Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself. Each time the function calls itself, it breaks the problem down into a smaller, more manageable piece. This process continues until the problem is reduced to a simple base case that can be solved directly without another function call. Finally, the results from all those smaller solutions are passed back up the chain to provide the final answer.
